This project provides the infrastructure and services for setting up Metabase and GCP resources.

docs.title: Key Architecture Decisions
docs.text: Component Selected Configuration Rationale GCP Project data-warehouse-492522 Host project containing BigQuery analytics warehouse and infrastructure. GCP Region us-west1 (Oregon) Optimal low-latency to California; standard Tier 1 GCP pricing (matches us-central1 costs). Domain & Ingress *.run.app (Cloud Run default) GCP-managed HTTPS via default Cloud Run domain; no custom domain or DNS configuration required. Container Runtime GCP Cloud Run Zero Kubernetes overhead; fully managed container lifecycle; integrated Cloud SQL proxy; native HTTPS. Instance Policy Min Instances: 1 Prevents cold-start delays and ensures Metabase background syncs, alerts, and scheduled pulses run continuously. Application Database Cloud SQL PostgreSQL Production-ready state store for Metabase (dashboards, queries, users, permissions). Never use the default embedded H2 database in production. Analytics Warehouse Google BigQuery Native driver built into Metabase. Authenticated via the Cloud Run attached Service Account (no JSON key rotation needed). Authentication Dual Auth: Google OAuth + Password Google Workspace OAuth restricted to @compiler.la for internal staff, plus password invites enabled for external stakeholders. Outbound Email Google Workspace SMTP Relay Reliable delivery of user invitations, password resets, and automated dashboard subscriptions. Secrets Management GCP Secret Manager Securely injects database passwords, encryption keys, and client secrets directly into container environment variables. Data Orchestration Cloud Scheduler + Cloud Run Jobs Serverless scheduling and per-source ingestion jobs. Low-cost and scales to zero. Data Modeling dbt Core Open-source analytics modeling; run as containerized jobs on Cloud Run to avoid dedicated VMs. Ingestion Method Puller Framework Python ingestion framework with auto-discovered Puller subclasses for each data source (e.g., Toggl).

docs.title: Production Cost Estimates
docs.text: This page provides an initial monthly pricing estimate for the production environment of the Warehouse project. These figures are based on minimal production-ready configurations and low request volumes.

docs.title: Monthly Estimated Cost Breakdown
docs.text: Resource Configuration Estimated Monthly Cost Cloud SQL (PostgreSQL) 2 vCPU, 7.5 GB RAM, 10 GB SSD $60 – $90 Cloud Run (Metabase) Min instances = 1, Low volume $10 – $30 Cloud Run Job (ingestion) 0.25 vCPU, 256 MiB, 1 execution/day $0 – $2 Cloud Scheduler 1 job (daily), Low volume $0 – $1 BigQuery Dataset only, minimal queries $0 – $5 GCS Storage < 1 GB total $0 – $1 Secret Manager 5 secrets (Metabase + Toggl tokens) $0 – $1 Total Estimated Monthly $71 – $130

docs.title: Key Assumptions & Notes
docs.text:
• Cloud SQL: Sized for a small team (approx. 20 users) to ensure smooth performance for Metabase metadata operations.
  • Cloud Run: Includes a minimum of 1 instance to eliminate “cold start” delays for users.
  • Cloud Run Job: The ingestion job runs once daily with minimal resources (0.25 vCPU, 256 MiB). Jobs are pay-per-execution, so costs are negligible at low frequency.
  • Cloud Scheduler: Triggers the ingestion job daily. Costs are based on a single low-frequency job.
  • BigQuery: Currently configured as a dataset with viewer access for Metabase. No compute queries have been run yet.
  • Secret Manager: Stores Metabase credentials (DB password, encryption key) and Toggl API credentials (api_token, workspace_id, organization_id). Free tier covers up to 100 secrets.
  • GCS Storage: Currently ingests ~333 KB/month. Costs are expected to remain negligible until data volume scales significantly.
  • Variability: These are estimates. Actual costs may fluctuate based on specific usage patterns and GCP pricing updates in the us-west1 region.

docs.title: Custom Metabase Docker Image
docs.text: This explains how the Metabase image connects to Cloud SQL PostgreSQL via Cloud Run’s built-in Cloud SQL proxy, using socat to bridge a Unix socket to TCP.

docs.title: Why a custom image?
docs.text: Metabase ships with an embedded H2 database by default. For production on Cloud Run we need it to use Cloud SQL PostgreSQL. Cloud Run mounts the Cloud SQL proxy as a Unix socket under /cloudsql/, but Metabase expects a TCP connection, so we need a bridge.

docs.title: Image layers
docs.text: metabase/Dockerfile starts from the official metabase/metabase image and adds only socat. No socket factory JAR, no classpath manipulation, no entrypoint patching.

docs.title: Entrypoint behavior
docs.text:
metabase/entrypoint.sh runs before the official Metabase entrypoint and performs these steps:

  1. Reads CLOUD_SQL_INSTANCE_CONNECTION_NAME from the environment. If unset, it auto-detects the instance name from the /cloudsql/ directory.
  2. Symlinks the Cloud SQL Unix socket into a known path inside the container.
  3. Spawns socat in the background to forward TCP port 5432 to the Unix socket.
  4. execs the official Metabase entrypoint so Metabase connects to 127.0.0.1:5432 as a normal PostgreSQL client.

If no Cloud SQL socket is present (e.g. local development via Docker Compose), the entrypoint skips all of the above and runs the official Metabase entrypoint unmodified.

docs.title: Terraform environment variables
docs.text:
Terraform injects the following environment variables into the Cloud Run service:

Variable Value Purpose CLOUD_SQL_INSTANCE_CONNECTION_NAME e.g. data-warehouse-492522:us-west1:metabase-db-40ee866c Tells the entrypoint which instance to bridge MB_DB_TYPE postgres Tells Metabase to use PostgreSQL MB_DB_HOST 127.0.0.1 Socat listens on localhost:5432 MB_DB_DBNAME metabase Database name MB_DB_USER metabase Database user MB_DB_PASS Resolved from Secret Manager Database password

Cloud Run also mounts the Cloud SQL volume at /cloudsql so the proxy socket is available at container startup. This is configured in the Terraform volume_mounts block.

docs.title: Local vs. production
docs.text: Environment Database config Behavior Cloud Run MB_DB_HOST=127.0.0.1 + CLOUD_SQL_INSTANCE_CONNECTION_NAME Socat bridges the Cloud SQL Unix socket to TCP 5432 Local (compose) MB_DB_HOST=postgres No Cloud SQL proxy — Metabase connects directly to the local PostgreSQL container. The entrypoint skips socat setup

docs.title: Upgrade path
docs.text:
When upgrading the Metabase version:

  1. Update the base image tag in metabase/Dockerfile
  2. Rebuild the image (docker compose build metabase)
  3. Test locally: docker compose up -d metabase and check logs for Successfully verified PostgreSQL
  4. Push a release tag to trigger CI/CD

docs.title: Deploying to Production
docs.text: This guide explains how the warehouse is deployed to production via GitHub Actions.

docs.title: Workflow Overview
docs.text:
The deploy.yml workflow supports three trigger modes:

Trigger Description Jobs Run Pull Request Any PR touching metabase/**, ingestion/**, or terraform/** terraform-plan (plan + comment) Tag Push Tags matching 202[6-9].[0-9][0-9].[0-9]+ (e.g., 2026.11.8) All jobs Manual (workflow_dispatch) Manual trigger from GitHub UI build-images, terraform-apply, health-check

docs.title: Concurrency
docs.text: The workflow uses a concurrency group (${{ github.workflow }} - ${{ github.ref }}) with cancel-in-progress: true. This ensures that only one run per branch/tag is active; newer runs cancel older ones.

docs.title: PR Plan (Pull Request Triggers)
docs.text:
When a PR touches any of the tracked paths, the terraform-plan job runs automatically:

  1. Authenticates to GCP via Workload Identity Federation (WIF).
  2. Fetches the latest release tag SHA from the GitHub API (falls back to "latest").
  3. Runs terraform plan with the latest image tags.
  4. Posts a summary comment on the PR using tf-summarize, showing the infrastructure changes in markdown. If a comment already exists, it is updated in place.

This gives reviewers a quick overview of infrastructure changes before merging.

docs.title: Automated Deployment (Tag Push)
docs.text: Production deployments are triggered automatically by pushing a release tag matching the pattern 202[6-9].[0-9][0-9].[0-9]+ (e.g., 2026.11.8, 2027.01.15). The tag must also be accompanied by changes in at least one of the tracked directories (metabase/, ingestion/, terraform/).

docs.title: Job Dependency Chain
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant Push as Tag Push
    participant Build as Build & Push Images
    participant Apply as Terraform Apply
    participant Health as Health Check
    participant Release as Release

    Push->>Build: Trigger
    Build->>Build: Build 3 Docker images
    Build->>Build: Push to GHCR (+ latest tag)
    Build->>Apply: Success
    Apply->>Apply: Terraform plan
    Apply->>Apply: Terraform apply
    Apply->>Health: Success
    Health->>Health: Check /api/health
    Health->>Release: Success
    Release->>Release: Create GitHub release
    Release->>Release: Generate release notes

docs.title: Step 1: Build & Push Images
docs.text:
The build-images job builds and pushes three Docker images to GitHub Container Registry (GHCR):

Image Dockerfile Tag ghcr.io/compilerla/warehouse/metabase:<sha> metabase/Dockerfile Commit SHA + latest ghcr.io/compilerla/warehouse/ingestion/base:<sha> ingestion/Dockerfile.base Commit SHA + latest ghcr.io/compilerla/warehouse/ingestion/toggl:<sha> ingestion/Dockerfile.toggl Commit SHA + latest

Details:

  • Build arguments: Each image receives IMAGE_CREATED (ISO 8601 UTC timestamp) and IMAGE_VERSION (tag name for release tags, or github.sha for manual triggers).
  • Layer caching: GitHub Actions cache (type=gha) is used for both cache-from and cache-to (max mode) to speed up subsequent builds.
  • latest tag: Every build also pushes a latest tag alongside the versioned tag, ensuring the most recent build is always easy to reference.

docs.title: Step 2: Terraform Apply
docs.text:
The terraform-apply job runs after build-images succeeds:

  1. Authenticates to GCP via Workload Identity Federation.
  2. Initializes Terraform and selects the default workspace.

  3. Runs terraform plan -out=tfplan -lock-timeout=5m with image tags injected via:

    • TF_VAR_metabase_image_tag — the metabase image tag
    • TF_VAR_ingestion_toggl_image_tag — the ingestion toggl image tag

  4. Applies the plan with terraform apply tfplan -lock-timeout=5m.

  5. Attaches a detailed plan summary to the job logs using terraform-plan-comment.

docs.title: Step 3: Health Check
docs.text:
The health-check job (a reusable workflow from .github/workflows/health-check.yml) runs after terraform-apply succeeds:

  1. Authenticates to GCP via Workload Identity Federation.
  2. Fetches the Cloud Run service URL for the Metabase service.
  3. Calls /api/health on the Metabase endpoint and expects HTTP 200.
  4. Fails the deployment if the health check returns a non-200 status.

This provides a basic smoke test to verify the service is responding after the rollout.

docs.title: Step 4: GitHub Release
docs.text:
If the trigger was a tag push (not a manual dispatch) and the health check passed, the release job creates a GitHub release:

  • Prerelease: false (final release)
  • Release notes: Auto-generated by GitHub (generate_release_notes: true)
  • Requires fetch-depth: 0 for full history to generate accurate notes

docs.title: Manual Deployment (workflow_dispatch)
docs.text:
You can trigger a deployment manually from the GitHub Actions UI:

  1. Go to the Actions tab → Deploy workflow → Run workflow.
  2. Provide the following inputs:
Input Description Example metabase_image_tag Docker image tag for Metabase v0.65.2 or a Git SHA ingestion_toggl_image_tag Docker image tag for Toggl ingestion abc1234 (Git SHA)

When triggered manually:

  • Image tags default to github.sha if not provided.
  • IMAGE_VERSION is set to github.sha (not a tag name).
  • The release job is skipped (it only runs on tag push).
  • The health-check runs after Terraform apply, just like automated deployments.

docs.title: When to Use Manual Deployment
docs.text:
• Rolling back to a known-good image tag.
  • Deploying a specific commit without creating a tag.
  • Updating only one image (e.g., Metabase) without changing the other.

docs.title: Required Secrets
docs.text:
The workflow requires these repository secrets:

Secret Purpose GCP_WIF_PROVIDER GCP Workload Identity Federation provider path GCP_WIF_SERVICE_ACCOUNT GCP service account for WIF authentication GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID Metabase OAuth Google client ID SMTP_PASSWORD SMTP password for email notifications

docs.text:
The workflow requests these GitHub token permissions:

Permission Used By contents: read Checkout code id-token: write GCP Workload Identity Federation authentication packages: write Push Docker images to GHCR pull-requests: write Post Terraform plan comments on PRs actions: read Read workflow run information contents: write Create GitHub releases (release job only)

docs.title: Variables
docs.text:
The workflow injects these Terraform variables:

Variable Source Description TF_VAR_metabase_image_tag Image tag input / latest tag SHA Metabase Cloud Run image tag TF_VAR_ingestion_toggl_image_tag Image tag input / latest tag SHA Ingestion Cloud Run Job image tag

docs.title: Terraform Version
docs.text: Terraform is pinned to 1.16.6 across all jobs (matching TF_VERSION in .devcontainer/Dockerfile).

docs.title: State Management
docs.text: Terraform state is stored in GCP (managed via the existing Terraform configuration). Plan locks use a 5-minute timeout (-lock-timeout=5m).

docs.title: Deployment Rollback
docs.text:
To roll back to a previous version:

  1. Quick rollback: Trigger workflow_dispatch with the previous image tag for the service you want to roll back (Metabase or Toggl).
  2. Tag-based rollback: Push a new tag pointing to the previous commit. The full pipeline (build → apply → health check → release) will run.

docs.title: Puller Abstraction
docs.text:
Every ingestion source implements a Puller subclass:

class Puller:
    source_name: str

    def pull(
        self,
        source: str,
        start_date: str | None = None,
        end_date: str | None = None,
    ) -> list[str]:
        ...

Subclasses set source_name (e.g., "toggl") and implement pull() to:

  1. Fetch data from the source (via API, CLI, or file)
  2. Transform it as needed (e.g., CSV conversion, column injection)
  3. Upload it to GCS via upload_to_storage()

docs.title: CLI Auto-Discovery
docs.text:
The CLI entry point (ingestion.main) uses discover_pullers() to find all Puller subclasses across the ingestion/ package at import time. No manual registration is needed — adding a new source package under ingestion/<source>/ with a Puller subclass is sufficient.

$ ingestion --help
Usage: ingestion [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

Data ingestion framework for Compiler's analytics warehouse.

Commands:
  toggl

$ ingestion toggl pull --help
Usage: ingestion toggl pull [OPTIONS]

Pull data for the given date range.

Options:
  --start TEXT  Start date (absolute or relative keyword)
  --end TEXT    End date (absolute or relative keyword)

docs.title: Date Range Resolution
docs.text:
The CLI supports flexible date inputs with three-level priority:

  1. CLI arguments — --start 2026-10-01 --end 2026-10-31
  2. Environment variables — INGESTION_START_DATE, INGESTION_END_DATE
  3. Defaults — "yesterday" for both

Relative keywords are resolved at runtime:

Keyword Meaning today Current date yesterday Previous date last-week Monday–Sunday of last week last-month First to last day of previous month 2026-10-01 Any valid ISO date

docs.title: GCS Upload
docs.text:
The upload_to_storage() helper supports two output modes:

Mode Trigger Path GCS BUCKET_NAME env var set compiler-data-lake/<source>/<YYYY>/<MM>/<DD>/<name>_<timestamp>.<ext> Local No bucket name <OUTPUT_DIR>/<source>/<YYYY>/<MM>/<DD>/<name>_<timestamp>.<ext>

For CSV files, a pull_date column is injected. For JSONL, a pull_date key is added to each record.

docs.title: Cloud Run Job Flow
docs.text:
Each ingestion source has a dedicated Cloud Run Job and Cloud Scheduler job:

Component Name Purpose Cloud Run Job ingestion-toggl Runs ingestion toggl pull with injected secrets and date keywords Cloud Scheduler ingestion-toggl-daily Triggers the job daily at 06:00 PST with --start last-month --end yesterday

The Cloud Scheduler passes relative date keywords (last-month, yesterday) — the CLI resolves them to actual dates at runtime. This means the job always pulls the correct range regardless of when it executes.

docs.title: Per-Source Isolation
docs.text:
Each source gets its own:

  • Cloud Run Job — isolated compute with its own CPU/memory limits
  • Cloud Scheduler job — independent schedule and retry policy
  • Service account — scoped IAM permissions (ingestion-runner SA with roles/storage.objectCreator and roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor)
  • Secrets — source-specific secrets in Secret Manager (e.g., TOGGL_API_TOKEN)

docs.title: Downstream Processing
docs.text:
Landed raw data flows through:

GCS → BigQuery (raw dataset) → dbt Core (Cloud Run Job) → BigQuery (staging + analytics) → Metabase

dbt models handle deduplication and transformation, ensuring the analytics tables in BigQuery are clean and queryable by Metabase dashboards.

docs.title: Container Images
docs.text:
All images are built and pushed to GitHub Container Registry (GHCR):

Image Path Base Ingestion base ghcr.io/compilerla/warehouse/ingestion/base:<sha> python:3.14-trixie Ingestion toggl ghcr.io/compilerla/warehouse/ingestion/toggl:<sha> ghcr.io/compilerla/warehouse/ingestion/base:<sha> Metabase ghcr.io/compilerla/warehouse/metabase:<sha> metabase/metabase:<tag>

Image tags use the git commit SHA (for tag-based deploys) or a user-provided value (for workflow_dispatch). OCI labels (org.opencontainers.image.version, org.opencontainers.image.created) are embedded in every image.

docs.title: Adding a New Ingestion Source
docs.text: This guide walks through adding a new data source to the ingestion framework. The framework uses a plugin-style architecture: you create a source package, implement a Puller subclass, and the framework auto-discovers it at runtime.

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text:
The ingestion framework consists of three layers:

  1. Base layer (ingestion.base/) — shared utilities: Puller base class, GCS/local upload, secret retrieval, CLI helpers.
  2. Source packages (ingestion/<source>/) — each source is its own Python package with a pull.py containing a Puller subclass.
  3. Entry point (ingestion/main.py) — discovers all Puller subclasses and dispatches CLI commands.

Auto-discovery means no manual registration is needed — just add a new module with a Puller subclass and it will be picked up automatically.

docs.title: 1. Create the Source Package
docs.text:
mkdir -p ingestion/my_source
touch ingestion/my_source/__init__.py
touch ingestion/my_source/pull.py

The package structure:

ingestion/my_source/
├── __init__.py      # Empty or re-exports (optional)
└── pull.py          # Contains the Puller subclass

docs.title: 2. Implement the Puller
docs.text:
Create ingestion/my_source/pull.py:

from ingestion.base.pull import Puller
from ingestion.base.gcs import upload_to_storage


class MySourcePuller(Puller):
    """Pull data from MySource."""

    source_name = "my_source"

    def pull(
        self,
        source: str,
        start_date: str | None = None,
        end_date: str | None = None,
        bucket_name: str | None = None,
    ) -> list[str]:
        """Pull MySource data for the given date range.

        Args:
            source: Source name (used for path prefix).
            start_date: Start date (YYYY-MM-DD).
            end_date: End date (YYYY-MM-DD).
            bucket_name: GCS bucket name (overrides BUCKET_NAME env var).

        Returns:
            List of uploaded file paths (GCS or local).
        """
        paths = []

        # Fetch data from the source (return CSV or JSONL string)
        data = fetch_data(start_date, end_date)

        # Upload to GCS (or local filesystem)
        path = upload_to_storage(
            data=data,
            source=source,
            filename="data.csv",
            pull_date=start_date,
        )
        paths.append(path)

        return paths


def fetch_data(start_date: str, end_date: str) -> str:
    """Fetch raw data as a string (CSV or JSONL).

    The framework injects a ``pull_date`` column/key into the output.
    """
    ...
    return csv_data

docs.title: Key Requirements
docs.text: Requirement Details source_name Class attribute identifying the source (used for CLI dispatch and GCS path). Must match the package name. pull() Must return list[str] — one entry per uploaded file. The list is logged but not otherwise consumed. data format String containing CSV or JSONL. Other formats are passed through unchanged (no pull_date injection).

docs.title: Real-World Example: Toggl
docs.text:
The Toggl source (ingestion/toggl/pull.py) is the reference implementation. It:

  • Defines source_name = "toggl"
  • Fetches 5 data types (timesheets, users, clients, projects, project-users)
  • Calls upload_to_storage() for each data type
  • Returns a list of 5 GCS/local paths

Each data type has its own filename constant (e.g., TIMESHEET_FILENAME = "timesheets.csv").

docs.title: 3. Handle Secrets
docs.text:
If the source requires API tokens or credentials, use the get_secret helper from ingestion.base.secrets:

from ingestion.base.secrets import get_secret

class MySourcePuller(Puller):
    source_name = "my_source"

    def pull(self, source, start_date=None, end_date=None):
        token = get_secret("my-source-api-token")
        ...

The helper currently reads secrets from environment variables. In production, secrets are injected into the Cloud Run Job’s environment from Google Secret Manager via the Terraform configuration (see Create Secrets above).

docs.title: Registering Secrets
docs.text:
Create the secret in Google Cloud:

gcloud secrets create my-source-api-token \
  --data-plaintext-file=/path/to/token \
  --replication-policy=automatic \
  --project=data-warehouse-492522

docs.title: 4. Add Dependencies (Optional)
docs.text:
If the source requires additional Python packages, add them as an optional dependency in pyproject.toml:

[project.optional-dependencies]
my_source = [
    "my-source-sdk>=1.0",
]

Add my_source to the setuptools packages list:

[tool.setuptools]
packages = ["ingestion", "ingestion.base", "ingestion.toggl", "ingestion.my_source"]

The optional dependency group (my_source) can be installed during the Docker build if needed:

RUN pip install .[my_source]

Add my_source to the devcontainer’s pip install so you can test locally:

RUN pip install .[toggl,my_source]

Update .devcontainer/Dockerfile and any relevant postCreate.sh or setup.sh scripts accordingly.

docs.title: 5. Test Locally
docs.text:
Run a test pull without GCP credentials (uses local filesystem mode):

ingestion my_source pull --start 2026-10-01 --end 2026-10-31

Check the output:

ls -la /tmp/warehouse-ingestion/my_source/

The files will be written to /tmp/warehouse-ingestion/ when no bucket is specified.

docs.title: Testing with GCS
docs.text:
To test GCS uploads locally, use --bucket:

ingestion my_source pull --start 2026-10-01 --end 2026-10-31 --bucket compiler-data-lake

docs.title: 6. Add Terraform Infrastructure
docs.text: Deploy the source to production by adding Terraform resources in terraform/modules/ingestion/:

docs.title: Cloud Run Job
docs.text: A Cloud Run Job runs ingestion my_source pull with the appropriate date range arguments.

docs.title: Cloud Scheduler
docs.text: A Cloud Scheduler job triggers the Cloud Run Job on a schedule (e.g., daily).

docs.title: IAM Bindings
docs.text:
The service account needs:

  • roles/storage.objectCreator on the data lake bucket
  • roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor for any source-specific secrets

docs.title: Secret Manager
docs.text: Add source-specific secrets (API tokens, credentials) to Google Secret Manager.

docs.title: 7. Deploy
docs.text:
Push a release tag (e.g., 2026.11.20) to trigger the CI/CD workflow. The new source is included in the base image (ghcr.io/compilerla/warehouse/ingestion/base:<sha>) since it lives in the ingestion/ package.

Deploy the Cloud Run Job and Cloud Scheduler separately via Terraform.

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• Created ingestion/<source>/pull.py with a Puller subclass
  • Set source_name to match the package name
  • pull() returns list[str] of uploaded file paths

docs.title: Cloud SQL Backup Verification
docs.text: This runbook covers how to verify, test, and troubleshoot automated backups for the Cloud SQL PostgreSQL instance used by Metabase.

docs.title: Backup Configuration
docs.text: Setting Value Automated backups Enabled Backup window 04:00 UTC daily Point-in-Time Recovery Enabled Transaction log retention 7 days Backup retention 15 most recent automated backups Replication log archiving Enabled

docs.title: List Recent Backups
docs.text:
gcloud sql backups list --project=data-warehouse-492522 --filter='instance:metabase-db-'

This lists all backups for the Metabase instance, including automated and ad-hoc backups.

docs.title: Check Latest Backup
docs.text: To verify the most recent backup succeeded, check the STATE column in the output. It should show SUCCESSFUL.

docs.title: Verify Backup Retention
docs.text:
The Cloud SQL instance retains the 15 most recent automated backups. You can verify by checking the count:

gcloud sql backups list --project=data-warehouse-492522 --filter='instance:metabase-db- AND TYPE:AUTOMATED' --format='value(NAME)' | wc -l

docs.title: Trigger an Ad-Hoc Backup
docs.text:
To create an on-demand backup (useful before major changes):

gcloud sql backups create --instance=metabase-db-<instance-suffix> --project=data-warehouse-492522

The <instance-suffix> is the random hex suffix appended to the instance name (e.g., 40ee866c). You can find it from the Terraform outputs or by listing instances:

gcloud sql instances list --project=data-warehouse-492522 --filter='name:metabase-db-' --format='value(NAME)'

docs.title: Scheduled Backup Window
docs.text:
Automated backups start at 04:00 UTC each day. The backup window is approximately 1 hour.

  • To check when the next backup is scheduled, review the WINDOW_START_TIME from the gcloud sql backups list output.
  • Backups run outside of the backup window are ad-hoc backups.

docs.title: Restore Procedure
docs.text:
Point-in-Time Recovery (PITR) is enabled with a 7-day transaction log retention window. You can restore the database to any point in the last 7 days using either a specific backup or a point-in-time timestamp.

Important: The restore procedure creates a new Cloud SQL instance (a clone). The original instance is not modified.

docs.title: Step 1: Identify the Target Backup
docs.text:
List recent backups to find the one you want to restore from:

gcloud sql backups list --project=data-warehouse-492522 --filter='instance:metabase-db-' --format='table(NAME, WINDOW_START_TIME, TYPE, STATE)'

Note the backup name and WINDOW_START_TIME.

docs.title: Step 2: Create a Clone Instance
docs.text:
Create a clone of the Metabase instance from the chosen backup:

gcloud sql instances clone metabase-db-40ee866c metabase-restore-<date> \
  --project=data-warehouse-492522 \
  --point-in-time="2026-11-09T05:16:30.131Z"

Or clone from a specific backup by using the backup name as the --restorable-disk-backup flag:

gcloud sql instances clone metabase-db-40ee866c metabase-restore-<date> \
  --project=data-warehouse-492522 \
  --restorable-disk-backup=projects/data-warehouse-492522/backups/<backup-id>

The clone takes a few minutes to provision. Monitor progress:

gcloud sql instances describe metabase-restore-<date> --project=data-warehouse-492522 --format='value(status)'

docs.title: Step 3: Verify the Restore
docs.text:
Connect to the clone instance and verify the data:

# Get the clone IP address
gcloud sql instances describe metabase-restore-<date> --project=data-warehouse-492522 --format='value(ipAddresses[].ipAddress)'

# Connect via psql
psql "host=<clone-ip> dbname=metabase user=metabase"

Check key data:

-- Verify the Metabase schema version
SELECT * FROM metababase_databasefield LIMIT 10;

-- Check recent dashboard entries
SELECT dashboard_id, title, position FROM metababase_dashboard ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 5;

-- Verify user count matches expectations
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM metababase_user;

docs.title: Step 4: Clean Up the Clone
docs.text:
After verification, delete the clone to avoid unnecessary costs:

gcloud sql instances delete metabase-restore-<date> --project=data-warehouse-492522

How the pipeline works: See the Deploying to Production guide for a detailed explanation of the workflow, build steps, and Terraform apply process.

docs.text:
• Push access to the compilerla/warehouse repository
  • Write access to the metabase/ directory (Dockerfile and entrypoint)
  • Write access to the ingestion/ directory (Dockerfiles and source code)

docs.title: 1. Update the Metabase Image
docs.text:
Edit metabase/Dockerfile to change the base image version:

FROM metabase/metabase:vX.XX.X

docs.title: 2. Update the Ingestion Image (If Applicable)
docs.text:
Edit ingestion/Dockerfile.base or ingestion/Dockerfile.toggl to change base images, dependencies, or source code:

# Base image
FROM python:3.12-slim

# Add any new dependencies
RUN pip install ...

If adding a new optional source, update pyproject.toml:

[project.optional-dependencies]
my_source = [
    "my-source-sdk>=1.0",
]

Update the Docker build to include the new dependency group:

RUN pip install .[toggl,my_source]

docs.title: 3. Push a Release Tag
docs.text:
Push a tag following the date format YYYY.MM.N to trigger the deployment:

git tag -a 2026.11.1
git push origin 2026.11.1

The Deploy workflow will then:

  1. Build and push 3 Docker images to GHCR (see how it works)
  2. Apply Terraform with the new image tags
  3. Roll out the new Metabase revision on Cloud Run
  4. Update the ingestion-toggl Cloud Run Job
  5. Run a health check against the Metabase service

docs.title: 4. Verify the Deployment
docs.text:
After the workflow completes, verify the deployment:

# Check the Cloud Run revision
gcloud run services describe metabase --project=data-warehouse-492522 \
  --region=us-west1 --format='value(status.url)'

# Verify the running image
gcloud run services describe metabase --project=data-warehouse-492522 \
  --region=us-west1 --format='value(spec.template.spec.containers[0].image)'

# Test the health endpoint
curl -f https://metabase-2xhfhhdfxq-uw.a.run.app/api/health

docs.title: Rollback Procedure
docs.text:
If a new version has issues, revert the tag and push a new one pointing to the previous version:

  1. Revert the Dockerfile to the previous Metabase version (or the previous git commit).
  2. Push a new tag to trigger a fresh deployment:
git checkout <previous-working-commit>
git tag -a 2026.11.2
git push origin 2026.11.2

docs.title: Quick Rollback (Manual Dispatch)
docs.text:
For a faster rollback without pushing a new tag, use workflow_dispatch:

# Trigger from GitHub Actions UI → Actions → Deploy → Run workflow
# Set metabase_image_tag to the previous working SHA or tag

docs.title: Revert to Previous Cloud Run Revision
docs.text:
If Terraform changes need to be reverted, you can also roll back to a previous Cloud Run revision:

# List revisions
gcloud run revisions list --service=metabase --project=data-warehouse-492522 --region=us-west1

# Route traffic back to a previous revision
gcloud run services update-traffic metabase --project=data-warehouse-492522 \
  --region=us-west1 --to-revisions=<previous-revision-name>=100

docs.title: Database Migration Considerations
docs.text:
Metabase may include database migrations with new versions. Be aware of the following:

  • Migrations run automatically on startup when the container starts.
  • Rolling updates ensure the previous version handles requests while the new version starts.
  • If a migration fails, the previous revision can be rolled back quickly.

docs.title: Pre-Upgrade Checklist
docs.text:
• Review the Metabase release notes (https://github.com/metabase/metabase/releases) for any database migration requirements
  • Ensure the Cloud SQL backup is recent and healthy (run a backup manually if needed — see Cloud SQL Backup Verification)
  • Ensure you can rollback to the previous version

docs.title: Post-Upgrade Checklist
docs.text:
• Verify Cloud Run revision is running the new image
  • Test the /api/health endpoint returns 200 OK
  • Log in as an admin and verify dashboards load correctly
  • Check that scheduled tasks (pulses, alerts) are running

docs.title: Ingestion Operations
docs.text:
This guide covers operational procedures for the ingestion framework: monitoring, troubleshooting, and ad-hoc pulls.

Adding a new source? See the Adding an Ingestion Source guide for a step-by-step walkthrough.

docs.title: View Job Status
docs.text:
gcloud run jobs describe ingestion-toggl \
  --project=data-warehouse-492522 \
  --region=us-west1

docs.title: List Recent Executions
docs.text:
gcloud run jobs executions list \
  --job=ingestion-toggl \
  --project=data-warehouse-492522 \
  --region=us-west1

docs.title: View Job Logs
docs.text:
# View logs for the most recent execution
gcloud run jobs executions logs \
  --job=ingestion-toggl \
  --project=data-warehouse-492522 \
  --region=us-west1

# Filter by execution name
gcloud logging read \
  "resource.type=cloud_run_job AND resource.labels.job_name=ingestion-toggl" \
  --project=data-warehouse-492522 \
  --limit=50

docs.title: Reviewing Ingestion Logs
docs.text:
The ingestion-toggl job logs stdout and stderr. Key log patterns to look for:

[TIMESHEETS] stderr: ...   # Subprocess output from compiler-admin
[USERS] stderr: ...
[PROJECTS] stderr: ...
[CLIENTS] stderr: ...
[PROJECT-USERS] stderr: ...

Each data source (timesheets, users, clients, projects, project users) logs its subprocess output separately.

docs.title: Triggering Ad-Hoc Pulls
docs.text:
To manually trigger an ingestion pull outside the scheduled daily run:

# Pull last week's data
gcloud run jobs execute ingestion-toggl \
  --project=data-warehouse-492522 \
  --region=us-west1 \
  --argument='--start' \
  --argument='last-week' \
  --argument='--end' \
  --argument='yesterday'

Or use absolute dates:

gcloud run jobs execute ingestion-toggl \
  --project=data-warehouse-492522 \
  --region=us-west1 \
  --argument='--start' \
  --argument='2026-10-01' \
  --argument='--end' \
  --argument='2026-10-31'

docs.title: Job Fails to Start
docs.text:
1. Check the service account permissions:
gcloud run jobs describe ingestion-toggl \
  --project=data-warehouse-492522 \
  --region=us-west1

Ensure the service account (ingestion-runner@...) has: - roles/storage.objectCreator on compiler-data-lake - roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor

  1. Verify secrets exist in Secret Manager: 
    gcloud secrets versions access latest \
  --secret=toggl-api-token \
  --project=data-warehouse-492522

docs.title: Pull Returns Empty Data
docs.text:
1. Check the source system (e.g., Toggl) for the requested date range.
  2. Verify the compiler-admin CLI is installed and accessible on PATH.
  3. Review job logs for errors from subprocess.run calls.

docs.title: Upload Fails
docs.text:
1. Check bucket permissions — the service account needs roles/storage.objectCreator on compiler-data-lake.
  2. Verify the GCS bucket exists: 
    gsutil ls gs://compiler-data-lake/

docs.title: Date Resolution Errors
docs.text:
The CLI validates that start_date is not after end_date. If you see a validation error:

ValueError: Start date (2026-10-31) is after end date (2026-10-01)

Use consistent keywords or explicit date ranges:

# Good: consistent keywords
--start last-month --end yesterday

# Good: explicit dates
--start 2026-10-01 --end 2026-10-31

# Bad: mismatched
--start last-month --end 2026-10-01

def register_source(group: click.Group, source_name: str, puller_class) -> None:
    """Register a source subcommand with the main CLI group.

    Each ingestion source (e.g., Toggl) provides a Puller subclass
    and is registered here so it becomes available as ``ingestion <source> pull``.

    Args:
        group: The Click group to register the subcommand on.
        source_name: The name of the source (e.g., "toggl").
        puller_class: A class that inherits from ``ingestion.base.pull.Puller``.
    """

    @click.command()
    @click.argument("action", type=click.Choice(["pull"]))
    @click.option("--start", "start_date", help="Start date (absolute or relative keyword)")
    @click.option("--end", "end_date", help="End date (absolute or relative keyword)")
    @click.option("--bucket", "bucket_name", help="GCS bucket name (overrides BUCKET_NAME env var)")
    def pull(action: str, start_date: str | None, end_date: str | None, bucket_name: str | None):
        """Pull data for the given date range."""
        resolved_start, resolved_end = cli.resolve_date_range(start_date, end_date)
        puller = puller_class()
        puller.pull(source=source_name, start_date=resolved_start, end_date=resolved_end, bucket_name=bucket_name)

    group.add_command(pull, source_name)

def resolve_date_range(start: str | None, end: str | None) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """Resolve start and end date strings to ISO format dates.

    Resolution priority:

      1. CLI arguments (if provided)
      2. Environment variables (`INGESTION_START_DATE` / `INGESTION_END_DATE`)
      3. Default: "yesterday" for both

    Handles both absolute dates (e.g., `"2026-10-01"`) and relative keywords
    (e.g., `"yesterday"`, `"last-week"`). When a relative keyword is used for
    a range (like `"last-week"`), both start and end are resolved together.

    Args:
        start: Start date string, env var value, or None.
        end: End date string, env var value, or None.

    Returns:
        Tuple of (resolved_start, resolved_end) in ISO format.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If start is after end, or if a keyword is not recognized.
    """
    # Resolve start
    if start is None:
        start = os.environ.get(_ENV_START)
    if start is None:
        start = "yesterday"

    # Resolve end
    if end is None:
        end = os.environ.get(_ENV_END)
    if end is None:
        end = "yesterday"

    # Handle range keywords that produce (start, end) tuples
    start_lower = start.lower()
    end_lower = end.lower()

    if start_lower in _RANGE_KEYWORDS and end_lower in _RANGE_KEYWORDS:
        # Both are range keywords — use the same one
        if start_lower == "last-week":
            return _last_week_range()
        if start_lower == "last-month":
            return _last_month_range()
    else:
        # Resolve individually
        resolved_start = _resolve_single_date(start)
        resolved_end = _resolve_single_date(end)

        # Validate
        if resolved_start > resolved_end:
            raise ValueError(f"Start date ({resolved_start}) is after end date ({resolved_end})")

        return resolved_start, resolved_end

    # If we get here, we have mismatched range/single keywords
    raise ValueError(f"Cannot mix range keyword '{start}' with single keyword '{end}'")

docs.text:
Upload data to storage, falling back to local filesystem.

Routing is determined by the effective bucket name:

def upload_to_storage(
    data: str,
    source: str,
    filename: str,
    prefix: str = "compiler-data-lake",
    pull_date: str | None = None,
    bucket_name: str | None = None,
) -> str:
    """Upload data to storage, falling back to local filesystem.

    Routing is determined by the effective bucket name:

      - If BUCKET_NAME env var is set (or bucket_name param overrides it) → GCS
      - If no bucket name is set → local filesystem (OUTPUT_DIR controls path)

    File path pattern (same for both GCS and local):
    `<prefix>/<source>/<YYYY>/<MM>/<DD>/<filename>_<timestamp>.<ext>`

      - For CSV files, a `pull_date` column is injected.
      - For JSONL files, a `pull_date` key is added to each record.

    Args:
        data: The data content to upload (string).
        source: Source name (e.g., "toggl").
        filename: Base filename (e.g., "timesheets.csv").
        prefix: GCS prefix / local directory prefix (default: "compiler-data-lake").
        pull_date: ISO date string for the pull_date column/key.
            Defaults to today's date.
        bucket_name: Optional explicit bucket name (overrides BUCKET_NAME env var).

    Returns:
        The full path of the uploaded file (GCS path or local file path).
    """
    output_dir = os.environ.get(_ENV_OUTPUT_DIR)
    bucket = _resolve_bucket(bucket_name)

    now = datetime.now(UTC)
    if pull_date is None:
        pull_date = now.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")

    blob_name = _generate_blob_name(source, filename, prefix)
    data = _inject_pull_date(data, filename, pull_date)

    if bucket is not None:
        return _upload_to_gcs(bucket, blob_name, data)

    if output_dir is None:
        output_dir = "/tmp/warehouse-ingestion"

    return _write_to_local(output_dir, blob_name, data)

def discover_pullers(
    base_package: str = "ingestion",
    on_error: callable | None = None,
) -> dict[str, type[Puller]]:
    """Discover all Puller subclasses across a package.

    Walks all submodules of the given package and collects classes that are
    subclasses of ``Puller``.  Modules that cannot be imported are silently
    skipped so that optional sources (e.g. ones that depend on packages
    that may not be installed) don't break the CLI.

    Args:
        base_package: The root package to scan (default: ``"ingestion"``).
        on_error: Optional callback invoked when a module fails to import.

    Returns:
        Dict mapping ``source_name`` to the Puller subclass.
    """
    results: dict[str, type[Puller]] = {}
    root = importlib.import_module(base_package)

    for importer, mod_name, is_pkg in pkgutil.walk_packages(
        path=root.__path__,
        prefix=f"{base_package}.",
        onerror=lambda err: on_error(err) if on_error else None,
    ):
        try:
            module = importlib.import_module(mod_name)
        except ImportError:
            continue

        results.update(_collect_pullers(module))

    return results

class TogglPuller(Puller):
    """Puller for Toggl data (timesheets, users, clients, projects, project users).

    Fetches data by invoking the `compiler-admin` CLI binary and uploads
    CSV files to GCS (or local filesystem if `OUTPUT_DIR` is set).
    """

    source_name = "toggl"

    def pull(
        self,
        source: str,
        start_date: str | None = None,
        end_date: str | None = None,
        bucket_name: str | None = None,
    ) -> list[str]:
        """Pull all Toggl data for the given date range.

        Args:
            source: Source name (used for path prefix).
            start_date: Start date (YYYY-MM-DD).
            end_date: End date (YYYY-MM-DD).
            bucket_name: GCS bucket name (overrides BUCKET_NAME env var).

        Returns:
            List of uploaded file paths.
        """
        paths = []

        # 1. Timesheets
        timesheet_df = _fetch_timesheets(start_date, end_date)
        csv_data = timesheet_df.to_csv(index=False)
        path = upload_to_storage(csv_data, source, TIMESHEET_FILENAME, pull_date=start_date, bucket_name=bucket_name)
        paths.append(path)

        # 2. Users
        users_df = _fetch_users()
        csv_data = users_df.to_csv(index=False)
        path = upload_to_storage(csv_data, source, USERS_FILENAME, pull_date=start_date, bucket_name=bucket_name)
        paths.append(path)

        # 3. Clients
        clients_df = _fetch_clients()
        csv_data = clients_df.to_csv(index=False)
        path = upload_to_storage(csv_data, source, CLIENTS_FILENAME, pull_date=start_date, bucket_name=bucket_name)
        paths.append(path)

        # 4. Projects
        projects_df = _fetch_projects()
        csv_data = projects_df.to_csv(index=False)
        path = upload_to_storage(csv_data, source, PROJECTS_FILENAME, pull_date=start_date, bucket_name=bucket_name)
        paths.append(path)

        # 5. Project users
        project_users_df = _fetch_project_users()
        csv_data = project_users_df.to_csv(index=False)
        path = upload_to_storage(csv_data, source, PROJECT_USERS_FILENAME, pull_date=start_date, bucket_name=bucket_name)
        paths.append(path)

        return paths

docs.title: Adding a New Ingestion Source
docs.text:
This tutorial walks through the complete end-to-end process of adding a new ingestion source. We will build a contrived acme_api source that fetches CSV data from a mock API endpoint and uploads it to storage.

Prerequisites: Follow the Getting Started tutorial to set up your local development environment.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
By the end of this tutorial, you will have:

  1. A new ingestion/acme_api/ package with a Puller subclass
  2. A working CLI command: ingestion acme_api pull --start ... --end ...
  3. Unit tests that mock the API client
  4. Optional dependencies in pyproject.toml
  5. The source added to the devcontainer for local testing

docs.title: 1. Create the Source Package
docs.text:
Start by creating the package structure:

mkdir -p ingestion/acme_api
touch ingestion/acme_api/__init__.py
touch ingestion/acme_api/pull.py

The package structure:

ingestion/acme_api/
├── __init__.py      # Empty or re-exports (optional)
└── pull.py          # Contains the Puller subclass

docs.text:
Create ingestion/acme_api/pull.py:

"""Acme API puller — fetches widget data from the Acme API."""

import pandas as pd

from ingestion.base.pull import Puller
from ingestion.base.gcs import upload_to_storage

FILENAME = "widgets.csv"


def fetch_widgets(start_date: str, end_date: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Fetch widget data from the Acme API.

    This is a contrived example. In a real implementation, you would
    use an actual API client or make HTTP requests here.

    Args:
        start_date: Start date (YYYY-MM-DD).
        end_date: End date (YYYY-MM-DD).

    Returns:
        DataFrame with raw widget data.
    """
    # Mock data for demonstration
    return pd.DataFrame({
        "id": [1, 2, 3],
        "name": ["Widget A", "Widget B", "Widget C"],
        "created_at": [start_date, start_date, end_date],
    })


class AcmeApiPuller(Puller):
    """Pull data from the Acme API.

    Fetches widget data and uploads it to GCS (or local filesystem).
    """

    source_name = "acme_api"

    def pull(
        self,
        source: str,
        start_date: str | None = None,
        end_date: str | None = None,
        bucket_name: str | None = None,
    ) -> list[str]:
        """Pull Acme API data for the given date range.

        Args:
            source: Source name (used for path prefix).
            start_date: Start date (YYYY-MM-DD).
            end_date: End date (YYYY-MM-DD).
            bucket_name: GCS bucket name (overrides BUCKET_NAME env var).

        Returns:
            List of uploaded file paths.
        """
        paths = []

        # Fetch data from the API
        df = fetch_widgets(start_date, end_date)
        csv_data = df.to_csv(index=False)

        # Upload to storage
        path = upload_to_storage(
            data=csv_data,
            source=source,
            filename=FILENAME,
            pull_date=start_date,
            bucket_name=bucket_name,
        )
        paths.append(path)

        return paths

docs.title: Key Points
docs.text:
• source_name: This class attribute identifies the source. It determines the CLI subcommand (ingestion acme_api pull) and the GCS path prefix.
  • Auto-discovery: The framework discovers all Puller subclasses at import time — no manual registration needed.
  • bucket_name: The optional bucket parameter lets callers override the BUCKET_NAME environment variable directly from the CLI.

[project.optional-dependencies]

Add acme_api to the setuptools packages list:

RUN pip install .[toggl,acme_api]

# ─── Cloud Run Job ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

resource "google_cloud_run_v2_job" "ingestion" {
  name                = local.job_name
  location            = var.region
  project             = var.project_id
  deletion_protection = false

  template {
    parallelism = 1
    task_count  = 1

    template {
      service_account = var.ingestion_service_account_id
      max_retries     = 1

      containers {
        name  = "ingestion"
        image = "ghcr.io/compilerla/warehouse/ingestion/acme_api:${var.image_tag}"

        args = ["acme_api", "pull", "--start", "last-month", "--end", "yesterday"]

        resources {
          limits = {
            cpu    = "0.25"
            memory = "256Mi"
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

# ─── Cloud Scheduler Job ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

resource "google_cloud_scheduler_job" "ingestion" {
  name             = "${local.job_name}-daily"
  description      = "Daily pull of the previous calendar month from Acme API."
  schedule         = "0 6 * * *"
  time_zone        = "America/Los_Angeles"
  project          = var.project_id
  region           = var.region
  attempt_deadline = "300s"

  http_target {
    http_method = "POST"
    uri         = "https://${var.region}-cloudrun.googleapis.com/v2/${google_cloud_run_v2_job.ingestion.name}:run"

    headers = {
      "Content-Type" = "application/json"
    }

    body = base64encode(jsonencode({
      "template" = {
        "template" = {
          "containers" = [
            {
              "args" = [
                "acme_api",
                "pull",
                "--start", "last-month",
                "--end", "yesterday",
              ]
            }
          ]
        }
      }
    }))

    oidc_token {
      service_account_email = var.ingestion_service_account_id
      audience              = "https://${var.region}-cloudrun.googleapis.com/v2/${google_cloud_run_v2_job.ingestion.name}:run"
    }
  }
}

iam.tf — IAM bindings for the service account:

# Allow the Cloud Run job service account to write objects to the output bucket.
resource "google_storage_bucket_iam_member" "object_creator" {
  bucket = var.output_bucket
  role   = "roles/storage.objectCreator"
  member = "serviceAccount:${var.ingestion_service_account_id}"
}

# Allow the Cloud Run job service account to read secrets at runtime.
resource "google_project_iam_member" "secret_accessor" {
  project = var.project_id
  role    = "roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor"
  member  = "serviceAccount:${var.ingestion_service_account_id}"
}

outputs.tf — values to expose from the module:

output "job_name" {
  description = "Name of the Cloud Run job."
  value       = google_cloud_run_v2_job.ingestion.name
}

output "scheduler_name" {
  description = "Name of the Cloud Scheduler job."
  value       = google_cloud_scheduler_job.ingestion.name
}

docs.title: 2. Create the Dockerfile
docs.text:
Each ingestion source gets its own Dockerfile that extends the base image and sets its own ENTRYPOINT. The base image (Dockerfile.base) handles the wheel build in stage 1 and installs it in stage 2 (without extras). The source image extends the base and installs only its own extras.

Create ingestion/Dockerfile.acme_api:

ARG PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
    PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \
    USER=compiler \
    USER_UID=1000 \
    USER_GID=1000

FROM ghcr.io/compilerla/warehouse/ingestion/base:latest

ARG USER_UID \
    USER_GID

ARG IMAGE_VERSION
ARG IMAGE_CREATED

LABEL org.opencontainers.image.version="${IMAGE_VERSION}"
LABEL org.opencontainers.image.created="${IMAGE_CREATED}"
LABEL org.opencontainers.image.url="ghcr.io/compilerla/warehouse/ingestion/acme_api"

# USER_UID / USER_GID are not inherited as ENV from base (base only sets them as ARG),
# but they are needed for BuildKit --mount uid/gid resolution at build time.
# All other ENV vars (PYTHONUNBUFFERED, HOME, USER, PATH, etc.) are inherited
# from the base image's ENV and need no re-declaration.

USER root
RUN --mount=type=cache,id=apt-archives,sharing=locked,target=/var/cache/apt/archives \
    --mount=type=cache,id=apt-lists,sharing=locked,target=/var/lib/apt/lists \
    apt-get update && \
    apt-get install --only-upgrade -y ca-certificates && \
    update-ca-certificates
USER ${USER}

# install acme_api extras on top of the base image's installed wheel
RUN --mount=type=cache,id=pipcache,target=${PIP_CACHE_DIR},uid=${USER_UID},gid=${USER_GID} \
    python -m pip install --user --upgrade pip && \
    pip install --user $(find /opt/wheels -name '*.whl')[acme_api]

ENTRYPOINT ["ingestion", "acme_api", "pull"]

No extras needed? If the source uses only the base dependencies (click, pandas, google-cloud-storage, etc.), omit the [acme_api] extra from the pip install line — the base image already has everything.

Source-specific extras: If you declared acme_api = [...] in pyproject.toml (step 3), reference it with [acme_api]. This installs only the source-specific packages on top of the base image’s common dependencies.

docs.title: 3. Create Secrets
docs.text:
Create the secrets that the job needs at runtime:

gcloud secrets create acme-api-token \
  --data-from-file=- \
  --replication-policy=automatic \
  --project=data-warehouse-492522
# (paste your token, press Ctrl+D)

Add a data source to read it (create secrets.tf in the module):

data "google_secret_manager_secret_version" "acme_api_token" {
  secret = "acme-api-token"
}

And reference it in the container env in main.tf:

env {
  name = "ACME_API_TOKEN"
  value_source {
    secret_key_ref {
      secret  = data.google_secret_manager_secret_version.acme_api_token.secret
      version = "latest"
    }
  }
}

docs.title: 4. Add the CI/CD Build Step
docs.text:
The deploy workflow builds images per-source. Each source needs its own Dockerfile and a build step in .github/workflows/deploy.yml.

Add the build step to the build-images job, alongside the existing toggl step:

- name: Build & push ingestion acme_api image
  uses: docker/build-push-action@c3c9e263c25d99ce0380d002d59b67737d91b0dc # v7.4.0
  with:
    context: .
    file: ingestion/Dockerfile.acme_api
    push: true
    tags: |
      ghcr.io/compilerla/warehouse/ingestion/acme_api:${{ env.TOGGL_IMAGE_TAG }}
      ghcr.io/compilerla/warehouse/ingestion/acme_api:latest
    cache-from: type=gha
    cache-to: type=gha,mode=max
    build-args: |
      IMAGE_CREATED=${{ env.IMAGE_CREATED }}
      IMAGE_VERSION=${{ env.IMAGE_VERSION }}

Image tag: The workflow currently uses TOGGL_IMAGE_TAG for all ingestion images. For a new source that shares the same release cadence, reuse this variable. If the source needs independent releases, add a new input like ingestion_acme_api_image_tag to the workflow_dispatch trigger and a corresponding env variable.

Add the Terraform variable to terraform/terraform.tfvars (or your preferred variable file):

ingestion_acme_api_image_tag = "abc1234"

Root variables: terraform.tfvars defines the runtime values Terraform uses. The var.* declarations in variables.tf at the root of terraform/ define the types and defaults. Add variable "ingestion_acme_api_image_tag" { type = string } to terraform/variables.tf if it doesn’t already exist.

docs.title: 5. Wire the Module into Root Config
docs.text:
Add the module to terraform/main.tf:

module "ingestion-acme-api" {
  source = "./modules/ingestion/acme_api"

  project_id                   = var.project_id
  region                       = var.region
  image_tag                    = var.ingestion_acme_api_image_tag
  output_bucket                = module.storage.bucket_name
  ingestion_service_account_id = module.iam.ingestion_service_account_email

  depends_on = [module.apis, module.iam, module.storage]
}

docs.title: 6. Apply Infrastructure
docs.text:
cd terraform
terraform init
terraform plan -lock-timeout=5m
terraform apply -lock-timeout=5m tfplan

After apply, the Cloud Run Job and Cloud Scheduler exist but won’t run yet — they need a deployed image.

docs.title: 7. Deploy to Production
docs.text:
With all the infrastructure in place, push a release tag to trigger the CI/CD workflow. The pipeline will:

  1. Build and push the ingestion/acme_api Docker image to GHCR
  2. Plan and apply the Terraform changes (binding the image tag to the Cloud Run Job)
  3. Run the health check on the deployed job
  4. Create a GitHub Release

Trigger the pipeline:

git tag -a 2026.11.20
git push origin 2026.11.20

Watch the run in GitHub Actions:

gh run list --repo compilerla/warehouse --workflow Deploy --json title,displayStatus,createdAt | jq '.'

Verify the deployment by checking the Cloud Run Job ran successfully:

gcloud run jobs describe ingestion-acme-api \
  --region us-west1 \
  --project data-warehouse-492522

And confirm data landed in GCS:

gsutil ls gs://compiler-data-lake/acme_api/
